episodes.title: Retinal Layers Explained: Bruch's to Photoreceptors for ODs
episodes.description:
Ever stared at an OCT B-scan and felt like you were reading a map in a language you almost understand? You're not alone — and this episode is the fix. In this clinically focused episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take licensed optometrists and eye care professionals on a precise, layer-by-layer tour of the posterior pole, from Bruch's membrane through the RPE, ellipsoid zone, outer nuclear layer, outer plexiform layer, and all the way to the inner retinal complex.

This isn't textbook anatomy for its own sake. Every layer we cover is tied directly to what you see in practice — drusenoid and fibrovascular PEDs, ellipsoid zone integrity as a visual prognosis marker, cystoid spaces in diabetic macular edema, RNFL thinning in glaucoma, and the OCT signatures that separate watchful waiting from urgent retinal referral.

We walk through two real-world clinical scenarios involving age-related macular degeneration — one guiding you toward AREDS2 counseling and structured follow-up, the other toward same-week retinal specialist referral — showing exactly how anatomical fluency drives confident, evidence-based chairside decision-making.

By the end of this episode, your OCT scans will speak to you differently. You'll know which bands to interrogate, which disruptions demand urgency, and why understanding retinal microanatomy is the single most transferable skill in posterior segment care.

This episode is designed exclusively for optometrists, optometry residents, and clinical eye care practitioners. If you're ready to make every fundus finding and every OCT report click into place, hit play now. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and CE content built specifically for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: The Optic Disc: Cup, Rim & the ISNT Rule Explained
episodes.description:
Are you reading the optic disc as carefully as your patients deserve? In this clinical episode of Focus Cast, we go deep on one of the most underread structures in routine optometric practice — the optic nerve head. Designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, residents, and eye care professionals, this episode breaks down the anatomy of the optic cup and neuroretinal rim, explains why the cup-to-disc ratio alone is not enough, and shows you exactly how to apply the ISNT rule at the slit lamp to catch the earliest signs of glaucomatous damage before your patient loses a single degree of visual field.

We cover the normal neuroretinal rim thickness pattern, why inferior notching is your earliest red flag, and how violations of the ISNT rule should immediately shape your clinical thinking. You will also get a practical differential diagnosis that separates glaucomatous optic neuropathy from AION, compressive optic neuropathy, optic neuritis, and large physiologic cups — because not every suspicious disc is glaucoma.

From chairside decision-making to OCT interpretation, pachymetry, 24-2 visual field analysis, and risk-stratified monitoring schedules, this episode gives you a complete, evidence-based clinical framework you can apply starting with your very next patient. We also discuss when to refer, how to document your reasoning, and which patient populations carry the highest glaucoma risk.

If you want to sharpen your optic nerve evaluation skills and build more confident, defensible clinical decisions around glaucoma suspects, this episode is essential listening. Subscribe to Focus Cast and visit focuslinks.in for more clinical episodes built specifically for eye care professionals.

---
